recipeCards.title: Moon Market Setting Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for table, paper, pencil, sketch, and imagination only.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Place one printed card, one pencil, and blank paper on the table. Say that each ingredient is a story idea, then invite a small sketch before writing.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine a moon market with quiet stalls, floating signs, and one tiny problem the setting can help show.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Moon Market setting recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: sky color ____________________, market sound ____________________, tiny sign ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Move one setting clue from the edge of the market to ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First the market looks like ____________________. Next the moon cart waits near ____________________. Last the setting feels ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace one plain place word with a more exact setting word: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch one stall shape, then label it: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, add one new Moon Market setting clue: ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Puddle Planet Mail Helper Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for inventing a helpful character with paper, pencil, sketch, and pretend messages.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Place the card on the table and ask for one helper sketch before any sentence. Keep every message pretend and every choice story-shaped.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine a puddle-planet mail helper who sorts pretend messages by color, shape, and mood.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Puddle Planet character recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: helper job ____________________, stamp shape ____________________, tiny worry ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Trade the helper's usual route for a puddle path toward ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First the helper notices ____________________. Next the pretend message points to ____________________. Last the helper chooses ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one exact character habit that readers can picture: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch the helper badge and write one character word: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, invent one new pretend message for ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Buttonwood Library Train Object Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for giving one paper-story object a clear job in a library train scene.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Set the card and pencil on the table. Ask the kid to sketch one small object, then write how the object helps the scene change.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine the library train rolls past shelves and needs one object to solve a small story mix-up.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Buttonwood object recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: object shape ____________________, shelf clue ____________________, train sound ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Give the object one surprising library job: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First the object rests near ____________________. Next the train shelf shifts beside ____________________. Last the object helps by ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace a vague object word with one exact noun: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch the object silently, then name its job: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, add a second helpful object called ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Teacup Weather Window Sensory Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for building a scene with color, sound, texture, paper, pencil, and imagination.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Place the card near a window or table view. Invite a quick sketch, then ask for one color, one sound, and one pretend texture.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine Teacup Town gets a message through the weather window, and the clues are all details a reader can picture.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Teacup Town sensory recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: window color ____________________, weather sound ____________________, tiny texture ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Swap the weather mood for a new story mood: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First the window shows ____________________. Next the room grows ____________________. Last the town hears ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one sensory word that makes the window scene clearer: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Point to a color, sketch a small square, and label it: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, write one more weather-window detail: ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Button Map Mix-Up Sequence Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for arranging a beginning, middle, and ending on paper.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Place the card on the table and draw three small paper boxes. Ask the kid to sketch one clue in each box before writing the sequence.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine a button map has its clues out of order. Choose the first clue, the middle clue, and the ending place.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Button Map sequence recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: first clue ____________________, middle turn ____________________, ending place ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Swap the middle clue with a clearer paper clue: ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one reason the middle clue belongs in that spot: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number the three boxes, then write only the first clue: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, retell the route with a new final clue: ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Ferry Harbor Revision Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free printable recipe-card writing prompt for improving one ferry-harbor sentence with paper, pencil, sketch, and imagination.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Place the card on the table and ask for one short draft line. Then invite the kid to add a clearer harbor detail.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine a tiny ferry crossing a lunchbox harbor. Write one draft line, then make the line clearer.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My ferry harbor revision recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: draft line ____________________, clearer detail ____________________, harbor sound ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up: Move the strongest detail closer to the beginning: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First my old line says ____________________. Next I add ____________________. Last my clearer line says ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Underline one exact word to keep in the revised sentence: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle one word with pencil, then rewrite only that word: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At another table, revise one ferry sentence about ____________________.
